hooks.text: Akrotiri is the Pompeii where nobody died.
Archaeologists found a prehistoric city with zero human bodies.
Why did the people of Akrotiri leave their homes?

title: Why Are There No Bodies in Akrotiri? 🤯
description: Discover Akrotiri, a Bronze Age city buried by a volcanic eruption where archaeologists found everything but the people.

beats.text: Akrotiri is the Pompeii where nobody died.
beats.visual: Panoramic view of the Santorini caldera formed by the volcanic eruption

beats.text: For centuries, many believed this buried city was a tomb.
beats.visual: Excavated ruins of Akrotiri covered in thick layers of volcanic ash

beats.text: In 1967, Spyridon Marinatos began excavating the volcanic ash.
beats.visual: Black and white portrait of Greek archaeologist Spyridon Marinatos

beats.text: He found three-story buildings and frescoes of swallows and red lilies.
beats.visual: The Spring Fresco from Akrotiri depicting swallows and red lilies

beats.text: But unlike Pompeii, no human remains were found in the ruins.
beats.visual: Empty excavated rooms and stone pathways of the West House in Akrotiri

beats.text: Preceding earthquakes likely warned the population to pack and flee.
beats.visual: Large ceramic storage jars known as pithoi left in the Akrotiri storerooms

beats.text: Today, archaeologists find only a ghost town frozen in time.
beats.visual: Modern protective roof canopy over the Akrotiri archaeological site

better_than_last: The emphasis for Beat 2 was corrected to exactly match its text, as 'mass tomb' was not in the spoken line.
